model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between Block Index and Sensitivity for 2-Fbit and 4-Fbit data. The horizontal axis, labeled “Block Index,” displays categories numbered from 0 to 63, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled “Sensitivity,” utilizes a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁴, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 10⁻⁵.  The chart contains paired bars for each Block Index; a dark blue bar represents “4-Fbit” data and a dark green bar represents “2-Fbit” data. For Block Index 0, the 4-Fbit bar reaches approximately 2.5 x 10⁻⁵, while the 2-Fbit bar reaches approximately 1.2 x 10⁻⁵. The height of the bars generally increases as the Block Index increases, though there is variation; the 4-Fbit bar for Block Index 63 reaches approximately 9.8 x 10⁻⁴, while the 2-Fbit bar for Block Index 63 reaches approximately 5.5 x 10⁻⁵.  No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between Block Index and Sensitivity for two different bit configurations. The horizontal axis represents Block Index, labeled from 0 to 63 in integer increments, with bars arranged sequentially. The vertical axis represents Sensitivity, labeled on a logarithmic scale from approximately 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁴, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 10⁻⁵. The chart displays sets of paired bars for each Block Index value, representing “4-Fbit” in blue and “2-Fbit” in green, according to the legend. For Block Index 0, the “2-Fbit” bar has a height of approximately 3 x 10⁻⁶, while the “4-Fbit” bar is absent.  Consistent with this,  “4-Fbit” bars begin to appear at block index 31. The tallest “4-Fbit” bar, found at Block Index 63, reaches a sensitivity of approximately 9 x 10⁻⁴.  The tallest “2-Fbit” bar, located at Block Index 47, reaches a sensitivity of approximately 4 x 10⁻⁵. The bars are sorted by ascending Block Index, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized.
